name: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram
charge: Rebellion against the men the Lord chose; seeking the priesthood also
summary: Korah of Levi, with Dathan, Abiram and On of Reuben and two hundred and fifty princes, famous in the congregation and men of renown, charged Moses and Aaron with lifting themselves above the congregation. The Most High was the one who chose them. They had the service of the tabernacle and it was not enough; they sought the priesthood also. The earth opened her mouth and swallowed them, and fire consumed the two hundred and fifty at their censers.
offenseFull: Korah, the son of Izhar, of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, of Reuben, rose up before Moses with two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown (Numbers 16:1-2). Two hundred and fifty three in all, and they were known and powerful men; their influence, because of who they were, is how they were able to persuade the people. The teaching will not let that detail pass. When division, heresies and offences come, the man who brings them is never the regular soldier or the regular officer; it is a brother who is well known and loved by the people, a man in a high position who was not faithful over the little he was given, and the ones who admire him leave with him. Of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them (Acts 20:30).

They told Moses and Aaron that they took too much on themselves, since all the congregation was holy, every one of them, and the Lord was among them, so why did they lift themselves above the congregation of the Lord (Numbers 16:3). They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, when the Most High was the one who chose them. Moses answered by asking whether it seemed a small thing to them that the God of Israel had separated them from the congregation to bring them near to Himself to do the service of the tabernacle, and whether they sought the priesthood also (Numbers 16:9-10). Only Levi could do the service of the tabernacle, and it was a heavy job in itself, and still it was not enough for them. Dathan and Abiram would not come up when called, because they wanted Moses’ spot: they accused him of bringing them up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill them in the wilderness, and of making himself altogether a prince over them (Numbers 16:12-13). Those same spirits are around today; what went on in the old time goes on now.
judgmentFull: The test was censers, since the dispute was over who might come near: the man whom the Lord chose would be holy (Numbers 16:5-7). Moses put the proof on the Most High: if these men died the common death of all men, the Lord had not sent him; but if the Lord made a new thing, and the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, then they would understand that these men had provoked the Lord (Numbers 16:28-30). As he finished speaking, the ground under them split apart, and the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, with their houses, all the men that belonged to Korah, and all their goods; they went down alive into the pit, and all Israel round about fled at the cry of them (Numbers 16:31-34). Fire came out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who offered incense (Numbers 16:35).

Their censers were taken out of the burning, because they had been offered before the Lord and were hallowed, and were beaten into broad plates for a covering of the altar, a memorial and a sign that no stranger who was not of the seed of Aaron should come near to offer incense before the Lord, and be as Korah and his company (Numbers 16:38-40). They envied Moses in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord, and the earth swallowed Dathan and covered the company of Abiram; they despised order and structure (Psalms 106:16-18). Peter calls such men natural brute beasts made to be taken and destroyed, who speak evil of the things they do not understand (2 Peter 2:12), and the teaching takes that at its word: they were made to be an example to us, so that we would not go against the leadership God set before us. Jude places everyone who follows them under the same sentence, perishing in the gainsaying of Core (Jude 1:11).

taught.title: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

text.text: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men:
And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown:

And they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the Lord?
Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.

Seemeth it but a small thing unto you, that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself to do the service of the tabernacle of the Lord, and to stand before the congregation to minister unto them?
And he hath brought thee near to him, and all thy brethren the sons of Levi with thee: and seek ye the priesthood also?
And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab: which said, We will not come up:
Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us up out of a land that floweth with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, except thou make thyself altogether a prince over us?

And he spake unto Korah and unto all his company, saying, Even to morrow the Lord will shew who are his, and who is holy; and will cause him to come near unto him: even him whom he hath chosen will he cause to come near unto him.
This do; Take you censers, Korah, and all his company;
And put fire therein, and put incense in them before the Lord to morrow: and it shall be that the man whom the Lord doth choose, he shall be holy: ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.
And Moses said, Hereby ye shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works; for I have not done them of mine own mind.
If these men die the common death of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men; then the Lord hath not sent me.

But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up, with all that appertain unto them, and they go down quick into the pit; then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord.
And it came to pass, as he had made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground clave asunder that was under them:
And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.
They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.
And all Israel that were round about them fled at the cry of them: for they said, Lest the earth swallow us up also.
And there came out a fire from the Lord, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.

The censers of these sinners against their own souls, let them make them broad plates for a covering of the altar: for they offered them before the Lord, therefore they are hallowed: and they shall be a sign unto the children of Israel.
And Eleazar the priest took the brasen censers, wherewith they that were burnt had offered; and they were made broad plates for a covering of the altar:

To be a memorial unto the children of Israel, that no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before the Lord; that he be not as Korah, and as his company: as the Lord said to him by the hand of Moses.
They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord.
The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
And a fire was kindled in their company; the flame burned up the wicked.
But these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption;
Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.
Now they that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah.
